relevance_note: Case report of one Japanese girl with HA20 due to a TNFAIP3 deletion ("a novel de novo 119 kb microdeletion containing only TNFAIP3"), plus a literature table (Table 1) of four previously reported HA20 patients with TNFAIP3 deletions.
method_note: Worked by reading the paper in full; a Python script in the scratch directory assembled the JSON, read Table 1 cells from the Markdown by row label and column position (output checked against the table by eye), and copied every span from the paper text. Table 1 has patients as columns (first line/header row is "Location"); columns are counted left to right: column 1 = "This report" (the index patient, labelled "patient"), column 2 = (Shimizu et al.^10), columns 3 and 4 = (Tsuchida et al.^8), column 5 = (Franco-Jarava et al.^9). Because rule 3 covers tables with patients as rows, the four previously reported patients are labelled "Table 1 column k" by analogy. Table spans are quoted from the row label through that patient's cell, so some Phenotype-row spans for columns 4-5 exceed 300 characters. Contradictions/uncertainties: (1) The paper writes the TNFAIP3 SNP as c.305A>G (implying A is the reference allele) but calls the father's G/G genotype "homozygous for the reference allele" and treats the patient's A/A as carrying "this variant"; recorded as the paper states (patient homozygous, mother II-2 heterozygous, no variant row for father II-1). The authors interpret the patient's apparent homozygosity as due to the deletion. (2) The deletion size differs by method: EXCAVATOR2 CNV analysis of WES data gave "a single de novo 187 kb microdeletion", the SNP array "a de novo 119 kb microdeletion"; one variant row was recorded using the array-validated ISCN string (the paper also prints ClinVar accession SCV001424911 for it). (3) De novo status: only the patient and father were tested by SNP array; the mother was genotyped only at c.305; recorded "de novo" because the paper states it and says the paternal allele was lost. (4) Grandparents had DNA extracted and appear in the Fig. 1D pedigree, but their number and results are not given in the text, so they get no rows. (5) n_patients_reported left null: the authors report "a case" first-hand and Table 1 lists four earlier patients, with no total stated; "five of 69 (7.2%)" is a literature-pool statistic. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients = true refers only to the four Table 1 literature patients; no earlier report of the index patient is stated. Supplementary Table S1 and Fig. S1 are not in the file, so the "abnormal condition of the autoimmune system" could not be specified (autoantibodies left not reported). Age at last evaluation left not reported for the index patient: "8-month-old" matches her age at diagnosis and follow-up continued at least 1 year after seton placement; vital status not stated. Checklist mapping choices: perianal ulcers (columns 2 and 5) counted as gastrointestinal ulcers; "thyroiditis" (column 4) not counted as autoimmune thyroiditis because "autoimmune" is not stated; plural "Upper respiratory infections" (column 5) counted as recurrent infections; "febrile episodes" and "Recurrent episodes of abdominal colic with fever" counted as recurrent fever; hepatosplenomegaly not counted as lymphoproliferation; headache and psychomotor delay not counted as CNS involvement; "not developmentally delayed" does not exclude CNS involvement; "afebrile" at the 8-month evaluation not treated as absence of recurrent fever; the fistula opening in the right labia majora not counted as a genital ulcer. Onset left null for literature-table features (the table gives onset only for the initial symptom group). Parents' features: the statement "no consanguinity or other significant family medical history" is not feature-specific, so all parent checklist items are not reported.
